subject: Pricing appendix & invoicing questions (HelioTech)
messages:
From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@heliotech.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@heliotech.com, Andrew Cho <andrew.cho@heliotech.com>
Date: 2026-10-03T08:19:00-07:00
Subject: Pricing appendix & invoicing questions

Hi Karthik,

Thank you for the updated order form. Our procurement team reviewed the Pricing Appendix and had a few practical questions we need clarified before legal can accept the redlines:

- True-up cadence: the appendix references an annual true-up but our accounting prefers quarterly reconciliations when minimum commits are involved. Can you confirm whether Redwood can support quarterly true-ups (pro-rata for partial quarters)?
- Invoice splitting: HelioTech needs the activation invoice separate from usage/true-up invoices and prefers invoices to map to entity A for activation and entity B for ongoing usage. Is that supported?
- Net terms: your doc lists Net45; can we request Net30 in the order form?
- Tax handling: can you confirm whether Redwood will gross-up for withholdings in cases where HelioTech is required to withhold tax? Also, we need a remittance address and entity name for invoicing.

I've attached a high-level procurement checklist and our PO template for reference. If useful, we can schedule a short call with our billing lead this week.

Thanks,
Sarah Liu
Procurement Manager
HelioTech
Attachments: Helio_Procurement_Checklist.pdf, HT_PO_Template.docx

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@heliotech.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-03T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing appendix & invoicing questions

Sarah — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Kimberly (Legal Ops) and Ben (Finance) to confirm the operational and legal side. Quick notes from my side:

- Quarterly true-ups: we can support quarterly reconciliations but need to confirm the billing entity mapping and whether you want pro-rata invoices for partial quarters.
- Invoice splitting: we typically support activation + ongoing invoices mapped to different legal entities, but we need to capture that in the Order Form (billing entity table) and in the invoice "Bill To" fields.
- Net terms: I can take Net30 to internal approvals; Kimberly, can Legal sign off on changing the order form payment terms to Net30 for HelioTech?
- Tax/gross-up: Ben/Finance — does Redwood have a standard gross-up posture for customer withholding or do we treat withholding on a case-by-case basis?

Attaching our most recent order form (v3) and the Pricing Appendix v2 that reflects the minimum-commit bands. I've also added a DocuSign placeholder link for the updated order form so we can iterate quickly: https://docusign.com/placeholder/HT-2026-79

If helpful, Sarah, Karthik here — happy to do a 20-min billing walkthrough with your team Thursday.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive
Redwood Inference
Attachments: Helio_OrderForm_v3.pdf, Pricing_Appendix_v2.xlsx

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@heliotech.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-04T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing appendix & invoicing questions

Hi all — thanks for the context. I reviewed the order form and Pricing Appendix and here are the legal redline items we need clarified/accepted before we can finalize:

1) Net terms: We can accept Net30 for this customer as a commercial concession, provided we capture the exception in the Order Form's Payment Terms section and include a 1.5% monthly late fee for unpaid balances after Net30. Please confirm HelioTech agrees to the late fee language.

2) True-up cadence: Quarterly true-ups are operationally fine, but we need the following in the appendix:
   - Definition of "quarter" and effective billing dates
   - Pro-rata calculation method for partial quarters (example formula and rounding rules)
   - Trigger for invoice issuance (e.g., within 15 days of quarter close)

3) Invoice splitting / entity mapping: We'll include a Billing Entity Table in the Order Form with fields: Entity Name, Tax ID, Remit Address, Invoice Type (Activation / Usage). HelioTech must confirm which entity corresponds to activation vs ongoing usage and provide tax documentation (W-9 for US entity or VAT registration for EU entity).

4) Withholding / gross-up: Redwood's standard practice is to pass through taxes and withholding unless a gross-up is contractually required. We can consider a gross-up but would need to document it in the Order Form Appendix and price for the estimated impact. Please indicate which approach HelioTech prefers.

5) Attachment & evidence: Please attach the consolidated PO and the W-9/VAT docs. I've attached a redlined Order Form (pdf stub) with inline comments on the Pricing Appendix (see Helio_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf).

Action items:
- Sarah / HelioTech: confirm quarterly true-up + pro-rata formula, identify billing entities and share tax docs (W-9/VAT).
- Karthik: update the Order Form Payment Terms to reflect Net30 + late fee and add Billing Entity Table.
- Ben: confirm accounting treatment and gross-up posture.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Legal Operations
Redwood Inference
Attachments: Helio_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@heliotech.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T12:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing appendix & invoicing questions

Quick finance take: we can do the proposed invoice sequencing — activation invoice mapped to entity A and quarterly usage/true-up to entity B — provided we receive the following prior to first invoice:

- Billing Entity Table populated with legal names, tax IDs, remit addresses
- Confirmed PO number for the activation invoice and PO lines referencing activation fee (if HelioTech uses POs)
- W-9 or VAT registration for the entity that will receive invoices in its jurisdiction

Gross-up: Finance's preference is to avoid gross-up unless HelioTech requests it and is willing to reimburse any incremental cost via a price adjustment. If HelioTech insists on gross-up, we'll need to model the uplift and reflect it in the Pricing Appendix.

I'll work with Billing Ops to prepare a sample invoice flow (activation, Q1 usage invoice, Q1 true-up) and circulate a billing example.

Ben Carter
Director, Finance (Revenue Ops)
Redwood Inference
